title: inbox: every decision waiting for a person, across features
description:
Result of `speccoder inbox`: every decision that waits for a
person, across the project's features, the most urgent first — the
person's work once the agents write the code.

items.description: The items, the most urgent first (see [`InboxItem::kind`]).

InboxItem.description: One decision waiting for a person.

kind.description:
What kind, in the order of urgency: `unknown` (the calls waiting in
the feature's journal could not be read — some may wait for you),
`approval` (a run waits on it),
`ruling` (a verified attempt is held: its tests reject an
alternative the spec allows), `gaming` (the monitor suspects a
shortcut), `stale` (proven against an earlier wording), `question`
(the spec leaves questions open), `review`
(requirements not approved on their current wording), `revise`
(changes requested on the spec), `stuck` (the
last attempt did not pass), `aside` (changes a run set aside),
`commit` (planning files a run cannot
read yet), `handoff` (every task done: review and hand it off) —
and a bug's `bug_confirm`, `bug_cannot_reproduce`,
`bug_unchanged_not_holding`, `bug_repro_weak`,
`bug_already_satisfied` (the registry: `speccoder_core::inbox::Kind`).

task.description: The task, when it is about one.

title.description: What to decide, in a line.

detail.description: What it rests on: the call, the reason, the changed requirement.

actions.description:
The decisions, the one that moves the work forward first; each runs
in the item's feature.

unverified.description: `unverified`: the feature's ticks and why each regression-only one is.

Action.description: One thing a person can do now.

label.description: What it does, in a few words.

why.description: Why, or what follows (shown beside it).

command.description: The equivalent command; `"…"` marks the input.

run.description: How an interface runs it; `None`: see `step`.

step.description:
How an interface takes it when it does not run it (`run` is `None`):
a view it opens, the person's own command, a line for their shell.

blocked.description: Why it cannot run now; `None`: it can.

input.description: What to ask for before it runs (`Describe the feature`).

confirm.description:
It leaves the machine (a push, a pull request) or cannot be undone
(a discard): what an interface says in a confirmation before it runs it.

id.description: What it is, independent of its wording ([`identity`]).

role.description:
A planning skill's part in its format's planning; `None` for
everything else.

Runnable.description: How an interface runs an action itself.

arguments.description: Its arguments (the input, when one is asked for).

oneOf.description: `speccoder run`, the feature or one task.

task.description: One task, or the feature's ready tasks.

agent.description:
This run's agent (`--agent`): an ACP preset or `native`; `None`
is the configured executor.

oneOf.description:
`speccoder run --converge`: the ready tasks, then the assessment of
the code against the spec as it is now, appending what remains.

Approve the task's waiting call: the one that was shown, refused
when another waits now.

digest.description: The digest of the call that was shown ([`crate::PendingCall::digest`]).

oneOf.description: Reject it (the input is the reason), bound the same way.

digest.description: The digest of the call that was shown ([`crate::PendingCall::digest`]).

oneOf.description: Tick the task on the person's word (the input is the reason).
Skip the task (the input is the reason).
Leave a note for the task's next attempts (the input is the note).

I did it: tick a step the person took on their word (`attested`;
the input, when given, is the reason).
Hint & retry: a note for the task (the input), then a new attempt.
Rule that a held attempt's tests are right (the input is the reason).

Record the person's review of requirements (the input is the
comment; required to request changes).

ids.description: The requirement identifiers; empty: every one not yet approved.

verdict.description:
`approve`, `request` (changes), `clear`; `answer` (ids: the
question) and `edit` / `edit-approve` (ids: the requirement) take
the input as the words.

oneOf.description: Tell a GitHub issue it is being specified as the current feature.

assign.description: Also assign it to the person.

oneOf.description: Record a quick change and, when `run`, run it.

request.description: The change, in the person's words.

checks.description: When it is done: its acceptance scenarios.

oneOf.description:
Commit the changes set aside before the task's run onto the
feature's branch, as the person's own.

Commit the setup a run stops on (an uncommitted lockfile, build
output not ignored) in the checkout.
Push the feature's branch and open (or update) its draft pull request.

Record a bug in the person's words (`speccoder bug`) and, when
`run`, reproduce it.

expected.description: What should happen instead (one or more).

unchanged.description: What must keep working (zero or more).

issue.description: The GitHub issue it comes from.

tests.description:
The person's own reproduction tests, one per expected statement
(`PATH::NAME`).

candidate.description: Someone else's fix to judge: a patch file or `pr:N`.

slug.description: Continue a bug the format's own bug step created.

oneOf.description:
Confirm (or, with `reject`, reject: the input is the reason) a
bug's reproductions, bound to the digest shown.

Keep an already-satisfied bug's reproductions as a regression test:
committed, the task attested (the input is the reason).
Continue a bug: reproduce again, or run its confirmed fix.

slug.description: A bug of the format's own bug structure, by slug.

oneOf.description:
Always Allow: approve the waiting command once and add exactly its
argv to `[commands] allow` (or `[sandbox] network_allow`).

Add a prefix to a prefix list, as the confirmation of its coverage
preview (refused when the preview changed or is incomplete).

digest.description: The digest of the preview the person saw.

oneOf.description: Decide the calls waiting in a run's batch together, each once.

verdict.description: Approve or reject (the input is the reason).

calls.description: The listed calls decided (a non-empty subset).

digest.description: The digest of the list the person saw.

resume_asking.description: Start the run's asking budget again.

oneOf.description:
Write, reject, ask again for, edit or settle a requirement's tests
at review (the input: the reason, the comment or the content).

Approve every approvable decision line, freeze the written tests and
start the feature's run, asking or on autopilot.

grants.description: The grant ids (object-bound grants) an autopilot run holds.

sheet.description:
The sheet's `sha256`: what the person saw approved and frozen.
Required from every interface but a terminal command.

oneOf.description: Add, delete or keep a review comment (the input: its words).

anchor.description: What a new comment is about.

oneOf.description: Send the comments as one revision turn.

ids.description:
The drafts the person saw (empty: every draft in the tray); a
draft sent already refuses the send.

oneOf.description: Undo the last revision turn: the documents back, byte for byte.
Code-view line comments as one nudge for the task's next attempt.

Write a story's acceptance tests at a Setup or Foundational task
(`revoke`: take the decision back) — a decision recorded in the
state directory, never an edit of the spec.

Install the bundled `speccoder` Spec Kit preset through Spec Kit's
own `specify preset add` (`update`: the installed one, replaced).

Plan a new feature through the format's own skills — the creating
skill, then toward the task list, then the check — stopping where a
person decides (`speccoder spec <skill> --through <t>`).

from.description: A new description, or the continuation after a stop.

oneOf.description:
Make `target` a project: the plan the person saw, bound to its digest
(`speccoder new`).

target.description: The folder, as the plan names it.

plan_digest.description: The digest of the plan on screen.

oneOf.description:
Undo the project speccoder created at the dispatch's root
(`speccoder new --undo`): to the Trash, or a revert of its commit.
Clone a repository of the person's with their git (their credentials).

Copy the bundled sample into the state directory and replay its
recorded run strictly (`speccoder sample`).

Run the sample's own checks, offline, in its copy (the sample's
end card, *Run the checks yourself*).
Each listed call, with one reason.

OracleOp.description: What a change to a requirement's tests does.

oneOf.description:
Write the tests (the author calls, the comparison, the red check,
the held-out set).
Drop one test (the input is the reason, required).
Write one test again (the input is the person's comment).
Replace one test's content with the person's (the input).
Say which reading of an ambiguous scenario is meant.

Reading.description: One of the two readings of an ambiguous scenario.

RunMode.description: How a run started from the review asks for a person.

oneOf.description:
*Ask on Risky Calls*: a call the policy asks about is asked inline,
as a run from the interface does.

*Autopilot*: nothing asks; a call the policy would ask about and no
ticked grant covers is refused for the run and listed afterwards.

CommentAnchor.description: What an anchored comment points at.

oneOf.description: A passage of a feature document.

quote_sha256.description: `sha256:<hex>` of the quote (filled when the draft is stored).

oneOf.description: A line of the spec's changes since the last commit.
A line of a shown visible test.

CodeComment.description: One line comment of the Code view.

oneOf.description: A new unit from a description.
The next skill after a stop, derived from the unit's files.

FeatureSource.description:
Where a new feature's description comes from. Later rungs add theirs
(an Explore brief, a promoted quick change) when they are built.

oneOf.description: The spec, the plan and the tasks.
Then the format's check of the planning files.

NewChoices.description: What the person chose; with the folder, everything the plan follows from.

idea.description: What they are building, verbatim (kept for the first feature).

no_preset.description: Leave out the speccoder Spec Kit preset.

Stack.description: A stack the plan can scaffold, or none.

oneOf.description: No scaffold: the person adds code.

How.description: How an interface takes a line.

input.description: What to ask for first (`Why it is skipped`); `None`: nothing.

text.description: The words the line gives already (a `--reason "…"` filled in).

confirm.description:
What to say in a confirmation first (it leaves the machine or
cannot be undone).

feature.description: The feature the line names (`--feature F`); `None`: the current.

subject.description: What it is about: a code, a task.

oneOf.description:
A command speccoder printed as a fix and can run as the person, in
the project folder, outside the sandbox — never one composed
elsewhere. Several argvs run in order, each only after the last
one succeeded (`a && b`).

interactive.description:
It reads the keyboard (a login): a terminal of the person's
own, not a panel.

outside.description:
What it changes outside the project, for a command that runs
outside the sandbox by its nature (`changes your global git
config`); `None`: it runs in the sandbox, writes confined to
the project and the package caches.

token.description:
The host's proof that it issued exactly these argvs; only a
host that runs commands sets it.

oneOf.description:
It must run in the shell speccoder starts from (`export NAME=…`):
nothing run elsewhere reaches that shell.

setting.description: The setting that stands for it (`model`), if there is one.

oneOf.description: Words for a person (`→ …`), or a command only they can complete.

why.description: Why it is not taken here; `None` for words.

View.description: A read-only place an interface opens instead of running a command.

oneOf.description: `doctor --bug-report`: the setup as a bug report, to copy.

`report --approvals`, `task approve|reject`: the calls waiting,
shown in full before a decision.
`explain CODE`: what a code means and how to resolve it.

ActionId.description:
What an action is, independent of its wording: its kind and what it
is about (the task, the skill, the issue). An interface finds an action
by this, never by its label.

subject.description:
What it is about: a task's id, a skill's name, an issue's number,
a review's `verdict` (`verdict:first id`), a command's words.

ActionKind.description:
What kind of action it is: one per [`Runnable`] kind (a run split by
whether it names a task), plus [`ActionKind::Command`] for an action an
interface does not run itself. Exhaustive at any one version; a new
kind arrives with its `Runnable` variant (the *adding a kind* contract
of `speccoder_runtime::actions::perform`).

oneOf.description: No runnable: the person runs the command.

SkillRole.description:
The part a planning skill plays in its format's planning, from the
format's adapter: what an interface finds "the create step" or "the
analysis step" by, without naming a format's skill.

oneOf.description: It leads toward the task list (`plan`, `tasks`).
It checks the planning files for consistency (`analyze`).

Unverified.description: A feature whose ticks are mostly regression-only, counted by reason.

counts.description: The reasons, the most frequent first.

ReasonCount.description: How many regression-only ticks had one reason, and which.

implemented_by.description: `already_passing`: the tasks that made the tests pass.

text.description: speccoder's words for the group (`7 had no user story`).
